summary: LETTERS FROM SPACE is an interactive educational website which looks at the history of the human-made machines left around the Moon, Mars and Deep Space. It does this by mission cards, some first person letters, a timeline of the missions and an interactive quiz. The user learns about the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Spirit and Voyager 1. It's a project that takes the real NASA mission data and combines it with a lot of storytelling to create a really engaging learning experience for younger people. The letters are all fictional of course, but they give each of the machines a voice and it's a very effective way of telling the story. It's all built in HTML, CSS and JavaScript and the aim is to get kids interested in robotics, engineering, planetary science and our continued exploration of the universe.
details:
LETTERS FROM SPACE is an interactive educational website aimed at introducing a school age audience to the history and science of human-made machines left in the Solar System.

The project is to take the history of space missions and turn it into a digital archive. You can go to three different destinations: the Moon, Mars and Deep Space. Each of those destinations has a number of missions and the associated machines (Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Spirit, Voyager 1 etc).

The site combines mission summaries with creative first person letters written from the point of view of each machine. These are fictional first person letters based on the actual mission history. You can also go through a chronological mission timeline and take an interactive quiz to test what you've learned.

Our objective is to demonstrate that equipment left behind is not just some forgotten piece of kit. It's a significant amount of engineering, scientific achievement and it's a series of milestones in our exploration of the Moon, Mars and the space beyond our Solar System. The stories of those spacecrafts are the stories of how technology has allowed us to understand those worlds.

The site was built using HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript in VS Code. It's a site with interactive missions, dynamic content and a multiple choice quiz. The current version is a front end educational site and doesn't use a database or any live spacecraft analytics.

Through storytelling and accessible science we hope to spark an interest in space exploration, robotics and science in the next generation.
